title: Probability & Statistics
why: ML models estimate probabilities and you must reason about uncertainty, base rates and whether a result is real.
explain: Probability quantifies uncertainty. Most ML models estimate a conditional distribution P(y | x). The core toolkit: expectation, variance, conditional probability, Bayes' rule and the common distributions (Bernoulli, Binomial, Gaussian, Poisson).

Bayes' rule says P(A | B) = P(B | A) P(A) / P(B). It explains why a test that is 99% accurate for a condition affecting 1% of people still produces mostly false alarms among its positives: the base rate matters. Naive Bayes classifiers are this rule applied directly.

Statistics asks how sure we are. Maximum likelihood estimation picks the parameters that make the observed data most probable; confidence intervals and hypothesis tests quantify sampling noise; and the bias-variance trade-off explains why simple models underfit while flexible ones overfit.
key_points: P(A | B) and P(B | A) are different quantities
Law of large numbers and the central limit theorem
MLE: choose parameters that make the data most likely (Gaussian noise gives MSE, Bernoulli gives cross-entropy)
pitfalls: Base-rate neglect: ignoring how rare the positive class is
Testing many hypotheses (or peeking at an A/B test) and reporting the one that looks significant

leetcode.why: Sampling from a discrete distribution with prefix sums plus binary search is how weighted sampling works in practice.
Reservoir sampling draws a uniform sample from a stream of unknown length.
The Fisher-Yates shuffle is how you correctly randomize training data.
O(1) random selection underlies mini-batch sampling and negative sampling.
Multiplying probabilities along paths (or summing log-probabilities) is the same trick Naive Bayes uses.

industry.q: A fraud detector catches 95% of fraud and flags 5% of legitimate transactions. Fraud is 0.1% of all transactions. Roughly what fraction of flagged transactions are actually fraud?
key_points: Use base rates: per 100,000 transactions, 100 are fraud
True positives = 95; false positives = 5% of 99,900, about 4,995
Conclusion: the threshold or model needs work, and costs should drive the decision

industry.q: Explain maximum likelihood estimation to a non-expert and name two models whose loss comes from it.
key_points: Pick the parameters that make the observed data most probable
Gaussian noise leads to mean squared error
Taking logs turns products into sums

industry.q: Your A/B test shows a 2% lift with p = 0.04 after checking the dashboard daily for two weeks. Do you ship?
key_points: Repeated peeking inflates the false-positive rate
Use a pre-set sample size or a sequential testing method
Look at the confidence interval and practical significance
